name: KSTDC Hotel Mayura Velapuri Restaurant
area: Temple Road, near Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
why_it_matters: The restaurant of the government-run KSTDC Hotel Mayura Velapuri, a five-minute walk from the Chennakeshava Temple — consistently flagged as the most reliable sit-down meal in Belur, a small Hoysala temple village with limited dining. Indian multi-cuisine menu, with a bar attached.
insider_tip: The menu and service hours are limited, so go at standard meal times — the food is tasty and the staff helpful. Its real advantage is the location, an easy walk from the temple. Cards, UPI and cash.
signature_address: KSTDC Hotel Mayura Velapuri, Temple Road, near Chennakeshava Temple, Belur, Hassan District, Karnataka 573115

name: India Coffee House
signature_dish: South Indian tiffin and filter coffee
why_it_matters: A simple vegetarian restaurant directly opposite the Chennakeshava Temple in Belur — the most convenient eatery for temple visitors, serving budget South Indian tiffin. It opens at 6am, which makes it the practical breakfast stop for early risers doing the temple before the crowds.
insider_tip: Right opposite the temple and open from 6am — ideal for an early dosa-and-coffee before darshan. Reviews flag mixed hygiene, so keep it to fresh, hot tiffin items. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: India Coffee House, opposite Chennakeshava Temple, Belur, Hassan District, Karnataka 573115

name: SLV Prasad Hotel
why_it_matters: A pure-veg South Indian restaurant near the Chennakeshava Temple — a popular post-darshan meal stop in Belur, known for dosas, idlis and vadas with fresh chutney and sambar. One of the handful of dependable veg eateries in this small temple village.
insider_tip: An easy walk from the temple — go for the South Indian tiffin straight after darshan. Simple, budget-friendly and consistent. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: SLV Prasad Hotel, near Chennakeshava Temple, Belur, Hassan District, Karnataka 573115

name: Shiva Prasad Grand
why_it_matters: A centrally located vegetarian restaurant in Belur town, about half a kilometre from the centre — a reliable veg option serving South Indian dishes, with masala dosa, veg thali and rava idli the standard orders for temple-circuit travellers.
insider_tip: A straightforward town veg restaurant — fine for a thali lunch between sightseeing. Central, so easy to reach on foot. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Shiva Prasad Grand, central Belur town, Hassan District, Karnataka 573115

name: Vishnu Regency Restaurant
why_it_matters: The restaurant at Vishnu Regency in Belur town — a hotel-attached dining option giving the small temple village another sit-down choice beyond the temple-front darshinis, serving South and North Indian food.
insider_tip: Useful as a calmer, hotel-attached alternative to the busy darshinis right by the temple. Standard multi-cuisine veg menu. Cards, UPI and cash.
signature_address: Vishnu Regency, Belur town, Hassan District, Karnataka 573115
